p.src: Our story now turns to the great city of Chang'an in Shaanxi, where emperors of successive dynasties had established their capitals. Since the Zhou, Qin, and Han dynasties, its three regions had bloomed like brocade, while eight rivers flowed around the city; it was truly a land of renowned beauty. At that time Emperor Taizong of the Great Tang had ascended the throne and inaugurated the Zhenguan era. Thirteen years had passed since his enthronement, and the year was Jisi. Peace prevailed throughout the realm: tribute arrived from every quarter, and all within the Four Seas acknowledged his sovereignty.

p.src: One day, when Taizong had taken his seat upon the throne and assembled his civil and military officials, the court audience ended and Chancellor Wei Zheng stepped from the ranks to memorialize: “All beneath Heaven is now at peace and every quarter is tranquil. We should follow the ancient custom, open the examination halls, summon worthy scholars, and promote men of talent to aid in governing and civilizing the realm.” Taizong said, “Your memorial is well reasoned, worthy minister.” He therefore issued a proclamation seeking men of talent and had it circulated throughout the realm: in every prefecture, subprefecture, and county, whether military or civilian, any scholar well versed in the classics, lucid in composition, and proficient in all three examination sessions was to proceed to Chang'an and sit for the examination.

Your son wishes to go and sit for it. If I should gain even some modest official post, bring honor to my parents and fame to my name, secure rank for my wife and privilege for my children, and shed glory upon our household, my ambition would be fulfilled. Go and take the examination, but be careful on the road; once you have obtained office, return quickly.”

p.src: As chance would have it, the procession passed the gate of Chancellor Yin Kaishan. The chancellor had a daughter named Wenjiao, also called Mantangjiao, who was still unmarried. A lofty pavilion had been festooned with colored silk, and she was casting an embroidered ball to divine her husband. At that very moment Chen Guangrui passed beneath the pavilion. The young lady took one look at Guangrui and saw that he was a man of exceptional bearing. Learning that he was the newly chosen Principal Graduate, she was delighted and cast down the embroidered ball, which struck Guangrui squarely upon his black gauze cap. Suddenly there arose the delicate music of mouth organs and flutes. More than a dozen maids and attendants hurried down from the pavilion, seized the bridle of Guangrui's horse, and escorted the Principal Graduate into the chancellor's residence to be married. The chancellor and his wife immediately came into the hall, summoned a master of ceremonies to conduct the rites, and gave their daughter to Guangrui in marriage. After bowing to Heaven and Earth and then to each other as husband and wife, they also bowed to the bride's father and mother. The chancellor ordered a banquet prepared, and they drank merrily through the night. Hand in hand, the two entered the bridal chamber together.

p.src: At the third watch of the fifth night-hour on the following day, Taizong took his seat in the Golden Throne Hall, and all the civil and military ministers hastened to court. Taizong asked, “To what office should Chen Guangrui, the new Principal Graduate, be appointed?” Chancellor Wei Zheng memorialized, “Your servant has examined the prefectures and commanderies under our jurisdiction. There is a vacant office in Jiangzhou; I beg Your Majesty to appoint him to that post.” Taizong accordingly appointed him governor of Jiangzhou and ordered him to make ready and depart at once, lest he miss the prescribed date. Guangrui thanked the emperor for his favor and withdrew from court. Returning to the chancellor's residence, he consulted with his wife, took leave of his father-in-law and mother-in-law, and set out with his wife to assume his post in Jiangzhou. They left Chang'an and took to the road.

p.src: It was late spring: gentle breezes stirred the green willows, and fine rain beaded the red blossoms. Guangrui made his way home, where he and his wife bowed before his mother, Madam Zhang. Madam Zhang said, “Congratulations, my son! And you have returned with a wife as well.” Guangrui said, “By the blessing of Mother's good fortune, your son had the undeserved honor of placing first in the examination and was commanded by the emperor to parade through the streets. As I passed Chancellor Yin's residence, a cast embroidered ball happened to strike me, whereupon the chancellor graciously took me as his son-in-law and gave me his daughter in marriage. The court has appointed your son governor of Jiangzhou, so I have now come to fetch Mother and take you with us to my post.” Madam Zhang was overjoyed and prepared for the journey.

p.src: After several days on the road, they came to the Wanhua Inn, kept by Liu Xiao'er, and lodged there. Madam Zhang suddenly fell ill and said to Guangrui, “I am unwell. Let us remain at this inn for two days while I recuperate, and then continue.” Guangrui obeyed. Early the next morning, he saw a man outside the inn hawking a golden carp, and Guangrui bought it for one string of cash. He was about to have it cooked for his mother when he saw the carp blinking its eyes. Guangrui exclaimed in wonder, “I have heard it said that when fish or snakes blink their eyes, they are certainly no ordinary creatures.” He therefore asked the fisherman, “Where did you catch this fish?” The fisherman replied, “I caught it in the Hong River, fifteen li from the prefectural city.” Guangrui took the fish to the Hong River and released it alive, then returned to the inn and told his mother what he had done. Madam Zhang said, “Releasing a living creature is a virtuous deed. It pleases me greatly.” Guangrui said, “We have already stayed at this inn for three days, and the imperial deadline presses upon us. Your son wishes to depart tomorrow, but I do not know whether Mother has recovered.” Madam Zhang replied, “I am still unwell, and the road is hot at this season. I fear my illness may worsen. Rent a room for me here so that I may stay awhile, and leave me some money for my expenses. You and your wife should go ahead to your post, and when the cool autumn weather comes, return to fetch me.” Guangrui consulted with his wife, then rented a dwelling and left his mother money for her expenses. He and his wife bowed farewell and departed.

p.src: The road was arduous; they traveled by day and lodged by night, until before they knew it they had reached the ferry crossing on the Hong River. There they saw two boatmen, Liu Hong and Li Biao, pole their boat to the bank to receive them. It must have been ordained by Guangrui's former-life karma that he should suffer this calamity and encounter these mortal enemies. Guangrui ordered his servant to carry the luggage aboard, and just as husband and wife were stepping onto the boat together, Liu Hong opened his eyes wide and beheld Miss Yin: her face was like the full moon, her eyes like autumn waters, her little mouth a cherry, and her slender waist a green willow. Truly, hers was a beauty that would make fish sink and geese fall, the moon hide and flowers blush. At once a wolfish desire arose in him. He therefore plotted with Li Biao, and they poled the boat to an uninhabited place. They waited until the dead of night at the third watch, then first killed the servant and next beat Guangrui to death, pushing both bodies into the water. When the young lady saw them kill her husband, she too made to throw herself into the river. Liu Hong seized her in his arms and said, “If you submit to me, all shall be well; but if you refuse, I shall end it with a single stroke of my blade.” The young lady could devise no means of escape, so she had no choice but to give temporary assent and yield to Liu Hong. The villain ferried the boat to the south bank and left it in Li Biao's charge. Then he put on Guangrui's official clothes and cap, took his credentials, and went with the young lady to assume the post in Jiangzhou.

p.src: Now the corpse of the servant slain by Liu Hong drifted away with the current. Only Chen Guangrui's body sank to the riverbed and did not move. A sea-patrolling yaksha at the mouth of the Hong River saw it and sped like a shooting star to report at the Dragon Palace. The Dragon King was just holding court when the yaksha announced, “At the mouth of the Hong River today, someone unknown has beaten a young scholar to death and abandoned his corpse on the riverbed.” The Dragon King ordered the body brought before him. After examining it carefully, he said, “This man is none other than the benefactor who saved me. How has he come to be murdered? As the saying goes, ‘A kindness must be repaid with kindness.’ Today I must save his life and thereby repay the kindness he showed me the other day.” He immediately wrote an official dispatch and sent the yaksha straight to the City God and local Earth God of Hongzhou to deliver it, requiring them to recover the scholar's soul so that his life might be saved. The City God and Earth God thereupon summoned a minor ghost and had Chen Guangrui's soul handed over to the yaksha. The yaksha brought the soul to the Crystal Palace and presented himself before the Dragon King.

p.src: The Dragon King asked, “Young scholar, what is your surname and given name? Where are you from? Why did you come here, and how were you beaten to death?” Guangrui bowed and replied, “This humble scholar is Chen E, courtesy name Guangrui, a native of Hongnong County in Haizhou. I had the undeserved honor of placing first in the recent imperial examination and was appointed governor of Jiangzhou, so I set out for my post with my wife. When we reached the river and boarded a boat, the boatman Liu Hong, coveting my wife, unexpectedly beat me to death and cast away my body. I beg Your Majesty to save me.” Hearing this, the Dragon King said, “So that is what happened. Sir, the golden carp you released before was none other than I. You are my benefactor and saved my life. Now that you are in distress, how could I possibly refuse to save you?” He had Guangrui’s body laid safely to one side and placed a complexion-preserving pearl in its mouth so that it would not decay, allowing him one day to return to life and avenge himself. Then he said, “For the present, your true soul may serve as a commander here in my underwater palace.” Guangrui kowtowed in gratitude, and the Dragon King held a banquet in his honor. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: Now Miss Yin hated the villain Liu so bitterly that she longed to devour his flesh and sleep upon his hide. Yet because she was pregnant and did not know whether she carried a boy or a girl, she had no choice but to submit to him for the time being. In what seemed but the blink of an eye, they arrived at Jiangzhou. The clerks, secretaries, gatekeepers, and runners all came out to welcome them. The subordinate officials arranged a banquet in the public hall to welcome and acquaint themselves with him. Liu Hong said, “Now that I have come here, I shall depend entirely upon your generous support.” The subordinate officials replied, “Your Excellency was the foremost graduate and possesses exceptional talent. All of us in your jurisdiction will benefit from your rule, so why be overly modest?” When the official banquet ended, everyone dispersed.

p.src: Time passed swiftly. One day, Liu Hong traveled far away on official business. At the residence, the young lady thought of her mother-in-law and husband and sighed sorrowfully in the flower pavilion. Suddenly she grew faint; pain seized her belly, and she collapsed unconscious to the ground, whereupon she gave birth to a son. A voice beside her ear admonished her: “Mantangjiao, heed my words. I am the Lord of the Southern Pole Star, and by command of the Bodhisattva Guanyin I have specially brought you this child. One day his fame will spread far and wide; he is no ordinary child. When the villain Liu returns, he will surely harm the child, so you must take great care to protect him. Your husband has already been rescued by the Dragon King. The day will come when husband and wife meet again, mother and child are reunited, your wrongs are redressed, and your vengeance is taken. Remember my words well. Awake—awake quickly!” Having spoken, the voice departed.

p.src: When the young lady awoke, she remembered every word. Clutching the child in her arms, she could think of no way to save him. Suddenly Liu Hong returned. The moment he saw the child, he wanted to drown him. The young lady said, “It is already late today. Allow me to wait until tomorrow before casting him into the river.” Fortunately, early the next morning, Liu Hong was unexpectedly called far away on urgent official business. The young lady thought to herself, “If this child is still here when the villain returns, his life will be forfeit. I had better cast him into the river now and leave his life or death to fate. If Heaven should take pity and someone rescues and raises him, perhaps I may meet him again one day.” Yet fearing that he would be difficult to identify, she bit her finger and wrote a letter in blood, setting down in full the names of his parents and the circumstances of his origin; she also bit off the little toe of his left foot to serve as a mark of recognition. Taking an undershirt she wore next to her skin, she wrapped the child in it and, finding an opportunity, carried him out of the residence. Fortunately, the government residence stood not far from the river. When the young lady reached the riverbank, she wept bitterly. Just as she was about to cast the child away, she suddenly saw a wooden plank drift up beside the bank. The young lady at once bowed and prayed to Heaven, laid the child upon the plank, bound him to it with a sash, tied the blood-written letter upon his chest, and pushed him out into the river to drift wherever the current might carry him. The young lady returned to the residence in tears. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: Now the child drifted downstream upon the wooden plank until at last it stopped at the foot of Gold Mountain Monastery. The abbot of Gold Mountain Monastery was a monk named Faming, who had cultivated truth, awakened to the Way, and mastered the wondrous secret of the Unborn. While he sat in meditation contemplating Chan, he suddenly heard an infant crying. Stirred at heart, he hurried to the riverbank to look and saw a baby sleeping on a wooden plank beside the shore. The abbot hastily rescued him. When he found the blood-written letter at the child’s breast, he learned the whole story of his origins. He gave the child the infant name River-Drift and entrusted him to someone to be raised. He kept the blood-written letter safely hidden away.

p.src: One day in late spring, while the monks were gathered beneath the shade of the pines expounding scripture, practicing Chan, and discussing profound mysteries, Xuanzang happened to confound a meat-eating, wine-drinking monk in debate. The monk flew into a rage and cursed him: “You wretched creature! You do not even know your own name or who your parents are, yet you come here playing your damned tricks?” Wounded by these words, Xuanzang entered the monastery, knelt before his master, and said with tears streaming from both eyes, “A human being is born between Heaven and Earth, receives life from yin and yang, and takes form through the Five Elements. Afterward I shall carry a basin of incense upon my head, rebuild the temple halls, and repay the profound kindness you have shown me.” His master said, “If you mean to seek your mother, take this blood-written letter and undershirt with you. Pretend merely to be collecting alms and go straight to the private residence of the Jiangzhou government office. Only then will you be able to meet your mother.”

p.src: Xuanzang accepted his master’s instructions, assumed the guise of an alms-seeking monk, and went straight to Jiangzhou. Liu Hong happened to be away on business. Heaven itself was bringing mother and son together, and Xuanzang went directly to the gate of the private residence to beg for alms. As it happened, Miss Yin had dreamed the night before that the waning moon became full again. She thought to herself, “I have heard no news of my mother-in-law; my husband was murdered by this villain; and my son was cast into the river. If someone rescued and raised him, he would now be eighteen years old. Perhaps Heaven will cause us to meet today—who can say?” While she was deep in thought, she suddenly heard someone reciting sutras before the residence and repeatedly calling for alms. Seizing the opportunity, the young lady came out and asked, “Where have you come from?” Xuanzang replied, “This poor monk is a disciple of the Venerable Faming of Gold Mountain Monastery.” The young lady said, “Since you are a disciple of the abbot of Gold Mountain Monastery…” She called him into the residence and gave Xuanzang a vegetarian meal. She observed his bearing and conversation closely and found him remarkably like her husband.

p.src: The young lady sent her maidservants away and asked, “Young novice, did you enter the monastic life as a child, or only after you were grown? What is your family name, and what is your given name? Are your parents still living?” Xuanzang replied, “I did not enter the monastic life as a child, nor did I do so after I was grown. When I tell my story, my grievance is as vast as heaven and my hatred as deep as the sea: my father was murdered, and my mother was seized by the villain who killed him. My master, Elder Faming, instructed me to seek my mother inside the Jiangzhou magistrate’s residence.” The young lady asked, “What is your mother’s family name?” Xuanzang said, “Her family name is Yin, and her given name is Wenjiao. My father’s family name was Chen, and his given name was Guangrui. My childhood name was River Float, and my Dharma name is Xuanzang.” The young lady said, “I am Wenjiao. But what proof do you have?” When Xuanzang heard that she was his mother, he fell to both knees and wept bitterly. “Mother, if you do not believe me, I have the letter written in blood and the undershirt as proof.” Wenjiao took them and examined them. They were indeed genuine, and mother and son embraced each other and wept. Then she cried, “My son, leave quickly!” Xuanzang said, “For eighteen years I have not known my own parents. Only this morning have I met my mother; how can you ask your child to tear himself away?” The young lady said, “My son, you must slip away at once. If that villain Liu returns, he will surely kill you. Tomorrow I shall feign illness and say that years ago I vowed to donate a hundred pairs of monks’ shoes, and that I must visit your monastery to fulfill the vow. Then I shall have more to tell you.” Xuanzang obeyed, bowed in farewell, and departed.

p.src: Now after the young lady had seen her son, her heart was divided between anxiety and joy. One day she suddenly pretended to be ill, refused food and tea, and lay in bed. When Liu Hong returned to the magistrate’s residence, he asked what was wrong. The young lady said, “When I was young, I once made a vow to donate a hundred pairs of monks’ shoes. Five days ago I dreamed of a monk holding a sharp blade, demanding the shoes, and ever since I awoke I have felt unwell.” Liu Hong said, “Why did you not tell me sooner about such a trifling matter?” He immediately took his seat in the court and ordered the assistant magistrates Wang and Li that every household in Jiangzhou was to provide one pair of monks’ shoes and deliver them within five days. The people all furnished their assigned pairs and delivered them. The young lady said to Liu Hong, “Now that the monks’ shoes are finished, what monastery is there nearby where I might fulfill my vow?” Liu Hong said, “Here in Jiangzhou there are Jinshan Monastery and Jiaoshan Monastery. You may go to whichever one you please.” The young lady said, “I have long heard that Jinshan Monastery is a fine temple. I shall go there.” Liu Hong at once ordered the two assistant magistrates, Wang and Li, to prepare a boat. The young lady took her trusted attendants aboard. The boatman pushed off, and they headed straight for Jinshan Monastery.

p.src: Xuanzang returned to the monastery in tears. After informing his master, he immediately bowed farewell and set out directly for Hongzhou. When he reached the Ten Thousand Flowers Inn, he asked the proprietor, Liu Xiao’er, “Years ago, an honored traveler named Chen from Jiangzhou left his mother at your inn. How is she now?” Liu Xiao’er said, “She did once stay at my inn. Later she lost her sight, and for three or four years she paid me no rent. Now she lives in a ruined tile kiln by the southern gate and survives by begging in the streets each day. That traveler has been gone for a very long time, and to this day there has been no word from him. I do not know what happened.” As soon as Xuanzang heard this, he asked his way to the ruined tile kiln by the southern gate and found his grandmother. The old woman said, “Your voice sounds very much like that of my son, Chen Guangrui.” Xuanzang said, “I am not Chen Guangrui. I am his son. The young lady Wenjiao is my mother.” The old woman asked, “Why have your father and mother not come?” Xuanzang said, “My father was killed by a bandit, and my mother was seized and forced to become the bandit’s wife.” The old woman asked, “How did you know to come looking for me?” Xuanzang said, “My mother sent me to find you. I have a letter from her here, as well as an incense ring.” The old woman took the letter and the incense ring, then wailed aloud, “My son came here in pursuit of rank and distinction. I thought he had betrayed all honor and forgotten his obligations, never knowing that he had been murdered. Yet happily Heaven has taken pity and has not allowed my son’s line to end, for today his grandson has come to find me.” Xuanzang asked, “Grandmother, how did you lose the sight of both your eyes?” The old woman said, “I missed your father and waited anxiously for him all day, every day, but he never came. So I wept until both my eyes went blind.”

p.src: Xuanzang knelt and prayed to Heaven, saying, “I, Xuanzang, am now eighteen years old, yet I have been unable to avenge my parents. Today, at my mother’s command, I have come to find my grandmother. If Heaven looks with compassion upon this disciple’s sincerity, restore sight to my grandmother’s eyes.” When he had finished praying, he used the tip of his tongue to lick his grandmother’s eyes. In a moment, both eyes opened and her sight was restored to what it had been before. The old woman looked closely at the young monk and said, “You truly are my grandson. Your features are exactly like those of my son Guangrui.” The old woman was overcome with both joy and sorrow. Xuanzang led his grandmother out through the kiln entrance and returned with her to Liu Xiao’er’s inn. He paid rent for a room where his grandmother could live. He also gave her money for expenses and said, “I shall return from this journey in a little over a month.”

p.src: He immediately took leave of the old woman and went straight to the capital. He found Prime Minister Yin's residence on the eastern street of the Imperial City and told the gatekeeper, “I am a relative and have come to see His Excellency.” The gatekeeper reported this to the prime minister, who said, “I have no monk among my kin.” His wife said, “Last night I dreamed that our daughter Mantangjiao came home. Could it be that our son-in-law has sent us a letter?” The prime minister therefore ordered that the young monk be shown into the hall. When the young monk saw the prime minister and his wife, he fell weeping to the floor before them, took a letter from inside his robe, and handed it to the prime minister. The prime minister opened it and read it through from beginning to end, then burst into loud sobs. His wife asked, “My lord, what has happened?” The prime minister replied, “This monk is your grandson and mine. Our son-in-law Chen Guangrui was murdered by a bandit, and Mantangjiao was forcibly taken by that villain as his wife.” On hearing this, his wife too wept inconsolably. The prime minister said, “Do not grieve, my lady. Tomorrow I shall report the matter to His Majesty and personally lead troops forth. I swear I shall avenge our son-in-law.”

p.src: The next day the prime minister attended court and memorialized the Tang emperor: “My son-in-law, Chen Guangrui, the top graduate in the imperial examinations, was taking his family to assume office in Jiangzhou when the boatman Liu Hong murdered him and seized my daughter as his wife; he has impersonated my son-in-law and held office for many years. This is a monstrous affair. I beg Your Majesty to dispatch troops at once and destroy the villains.” The Tang emperor was enraged by the memorial. He immediately mobilized sixty thousand imperial guards and ordered Prime Minister Yin to command them. The prime minister received the decree and left the court, mustered the troops on the drill ground, and marched directly toward Jiangzhou. Traveling by day and lodging by night, setting out before the stars had faded and the birds begun to fly, they soon reached Jiangzhou, where all Prime Minister Yin's forces made camp on the northern bank. That very night, he sent an urgent gold-badge summons to the assistant prefect and the judicial officer of Jiangzhou. When they arrived, the prime minister explained the affair, ordered them to muster troops in support, and crossed the river together with them. Before dawn, they surrounded Liu Hong's yamen. Liu Hong was still dreaming when a cannon boomed and gongs and drums sounded together. The soldiers stormed his private quarters, and before he could react, he was seized. The prime minister issued a military order to bind Liu Hong and all his accomplices and take them to the execution ground, while the rest of the army withdrew to camp outside the city.

p.src: The prime minister went straight into the yamen and seated himself in the main hall, then asked that his daughter come out to meet him. She wished to come out, but was too ashamed to face her father and tried to hang herself. When Xuanzang heard of this, he rushed to save his mother, knelt before her, and said, “Your son has come here with Grandfather at the head of an army to avenge Father. Now that the villain has been captured, Mother, why do you seek death instead? If you die, Mother, how could your child go on living?” The prime minister also entered the yamen and sought to comfort her. She said, “I have heard it said that a woman must remain faithful to one husband until death. My beloved husband was murdered by that villain; how could I shamelessly submit to the murderer? Only because I carried his unborn child was I forced to swallow my shame and cling to life. Now, by good fortune, my son is grown, and I have seen my aged father lead troops to avenge us. How can I, your daughter, have the face to meet you? Only by dying can I repay my husband.” The prime minister said, “You did not forsake your constancy because fortune changed; everything you did was forced upon you. What cause have you for shame?” Father and daughter embraced and wept, while Xuanzang too sobbed without cease. Wiping away his tears, the prime minister said, “You two must grieve no more for now; I have captured our mortal enemy, and must now go see that he is dealt with.” He rose at once and went to the execution ground. Just then, the assistant prefect of Jiangzhou also sent scouts who captured the river bandit Li Biao and brought him in under guard. The prime minister was delighted. He ordered the military jailers to bring Liu Hong and Li Biao forward and give each a hundred heavy blows. Their confessions were taken, and they admitted how years before they had conspired to murder Chen Guangrui. Li Biao was first nailed to a wooden donkey, paraded to the marketplace, sliced to death by a thousand cuts, and beheaded, his head displayed as a warning to all. Liu Hong was taken to the Hongjiang ferry, the place where he had killed Chen Guangrui years before. The prime minister, his daughter, and Xuanzang went in person to the riverbank, where they made offerings toward the heavens. Liu Hong's heart and liver were cut from him alive and offered in sacrifice to Guangrui, and a funerary prayer was burned.

Li Biao was first nailed to a wooden donkey, paraded to the marketplace, sliced to death by a thousand cuts, and beheaded, his head displayed as a warning to all.
Liu Hong was taken to the Hongjiang ferry, the place where he had killed Chen Guangrui years before.

The prime minister, his daughter, and Xuanzang went in person to the riverbank, where they made offerings toward the heavens. Liu Hong's heart and liver were cut from him alive and offered in sacrifice to Guangrui, and a funerary prayer was burned.

p.src: As the three gazed across the river and wept bitterly, their lamentations disturbed the Water Palace, and a sea-patrolling yaksha presented the funerary prayer to the Dragon King. After reading it, the Dragon King sent Turtle Marshal to summon Guangrui and said, “Congratulations, sir, congratulations! Your wife, your son, and your father-in-law are now all gathered on the riverbank to make offerings to you. I shall now send you back to life. I shall also present you with one wish-fulfilling pearl, two rolling-plate pearls, ten bolts of twisted silk, and a jade belt set with luminous pearls. This very day, husband and wife, mother and son, may all be reunited.” Guangrui bowed repeatedly in gratitude. The Dragon King then ordered a yaksha to carry Guangrui's body out to the river mouth and restore his soul to it. The yaksha received the order and departed.

p.src: Now after Lady Yin had wept and made offerings to her husband, she again tried to throw herself into the river and die, but Xuanzang desperately seized and held her back. Amid this confusion, they suddenly saw a corpse floating upon the water and drifting close to the riverbank. She hurried forward to look and recognized her husband's body, whereupon she wailed more bitterly than ever. Everyone came to look. Before their eyes Guangrui unclenched his fists and stretched out his legs; his body gradually began to move, and suddenly he pushed himself upright and sat up. Everyone was overwhelmed with astonishment. Guangrui opened his eyes and at once saw Lady Yin, his father-in-law Prime Minister Yin, and the young monk all beside him, weeping. Guangrui asked, “Why are you all here?” His wife replied, “After you were murdered by the villains, I gave birth to this son. By good fortune, the elder of Gold Mountain Monastery raised him to adulthood. He found me and was reunited with me, and I sent him to seek his maternal grandfather. When Father learned the truth, he reported it to the court and led troops here to capture the villains. Just now, he cut out the murderer's heart and liver alive and offered them toward the heavens in sacrifice to you, my husband. But how is it that you have now returned to life?” Guangrui said, “It is all because, years ago at the Ten Thousand Flowers Inn, you and I bought that golden carp and set it free. Who could have known that the carp was the Dragon King of this place? Later, when the traitorous villains pushed me into the water, it was entirely thanks to him that I was saved. Just now he granted me life again and gave me treasures, all of which I have upon me. Never did I imagine that you had borne me this son, or that my father-in-law would avenge me. Truly, our sorrows are ended and joy has come; no happiness could be greater.”

p.src: When the officials heard the news, they all came to offer their congratulations. The prime minister ordered a banquet prepared to thank the local officials. That same day, the army set out on its return journey. When they reached the Ten Thousand Flowers Inn, the prime minister gave orders to make camp. Guangrui then went with Xuanzang to the Liu Family Inn to find his mother. That night the old woman had dreamed of a withered tree bursting into bloom, while magpies chattered again and again behind the house. She thought, “Could my grandson be coming?” Before she had finished speaking, Guangrui and his son arrived together outside the inn door. The young monk pointed and said, “Is that not my grandmother?” When Guangrui saw his aged mother, he hurriedly fell to his knees before her. Mother and son embraced and wept bitterly, and he told her the whole story of what had happened. After settling the bill with the inn servant, they set out and returned to the capital. Upon entering the prime minister's residence, Guangrui, his wife, his mother, and Xuanzang all went to pay their respects to the prime minister's wife. Her joy knew no bounds, and she ordered the household servants to prepare a grand celebratory feast. The prime minister said, “Today's feast may well be called the Reunion Banquet.” The whole family was truly filled with joy.

p.src: At the morning court the next day, the Tang emperor ascended the throne. Chancellor Yin stepped forward from the ranks and reported the entire affair in full detail, also recommending Guangrui as a man of talent fit for high office. The Tang emperor approved his memorial and immediately appointed Chen E to the post of academician, charging him to attend court and assist in governing the realm. Xuanzang resolved to devote himself to meditation and was sent to cultivate the Way at Hongfu Monastery. Later, Miss Yin did in the end calmly take her own life. Xuanzang himself went to Jinshan Monastery to repay the kindness of Elder Faming.
